away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined and will return to the crease for the ninth time in Minnesota's first 10 games. That said, the increased playing time hasn't hindered the 23-year-old Wallstedt, who has a dazzling 1.99 GAA and .922 SV% in eight games (1-1-0). Still, Minnesota enters Tuesday's matchup as slight +116 road underdogs against a 6-1-1 Edmonton Oilers team that is clicking offensively (4.63 GF/GP).

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: The Oilers have struggled between the pipes in recent seasons, but Devon Levi's play has been encouraging early in the 2026-27 season. That said, Levi is coming off his first loss as an Oiler, allowing three goals on 24 shots (.875 SV%) in a 4-2 loss to the Utah Mammoth. The 24-year-old goalie has allowed two or fewer goals in three of five games this season (4-1-0), posting a 2.83 GAA and .898 SV%. The Oilers enter Tuesday's contest as -129 home favourites against a 6-2-1 Minnesota Wild team.

away.name: Daniil Tarasov
away.news: Tarasov has been exceptional in limited action this season and appears to be getting more playing time as a result, as he will tend the twine for the third time in Detroit's last five games. The 27-year-old goalie saved 17 of 18 shots (.944 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 2-1 win over the Philadelphia Flyers. He has a 0.80 GAA and a .965 SV% in three appearances (1-0-1).

home.name: Philipp Grubauer
home.news: Seattle is off to a solid 5-3-1 start this season and has received encouraging goaltending from Grubauer, who has never lived up to being the team's number-one goalie. That said, Grubauer will hope to bounce back after a season-worst performance in which he allowed four goals on 35 shots (.886 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning. The 34-year-old German goalie has a 2.71 GAA and .910 SV% in five games (2-1-1). The Kraken enter Tuesday's contest as +102 home underdogs against a Detroit Red Wings team on a two-game winning streak.

away.name: Pyotr Kochetkov
away.news: Hurricanes Head Coach Rod Brind'Amour started Brandon Bussi in the first two games of the season, but has leaned a bit more heavily on Kochetkov in recent games. The 27-year-old goalie returns to the crease on Tuesday for his sixth start in his last nine games and, deservedly, after posting a tremendous undefeated 5-0-0 record with a 1.78 GAA and .912 SV%. The Hurricanes enter Tuesday's action as enormous -294 road favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team that has scored two or fewer goals in seven consecutive games (0-6-1).

home.name: Leevi Merilainen
home.news: Kevin Lankinen has started the 2025-26 season abysmal, posting a dreadful 6.40 GAA and .807 SV% in seven outings (1-6-0). As a result, the Canucks have increasingly turned to Merilainen, who has been the more reliable goalie. The 24-year-old Merilainen was solid in his most recent outing, saving 36 of 39 shots (.923 SV%), but came up short in a 3-2 overtime loss to the Florida Panthers. In six appearances this season (1-1-1), Merilainen has a solid 2.51 GAA and .925 SV%. Still, the Canucks enter Tuesday's matchup as significant +253 home underdogs against the 7-2-1 Carolina Hurricanes.

away.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
away.news: Tampa Bay is on a hot 6-1-0 run, and they've done it without needing Vasilevskiy, the reigning Vezina Trophy winner, to be spectacular. Vasilevskiy has uncharacteristically allowed three goals in each of his last three games (2-1-0). The 32-year-old goalie has a 2.53 GAA and .886 SV% in six games this season (4-2-0). Tampa Bay enters Tuesday's contest as slight -108 road favourites against a Vegas Golden Knights team that has outscored opponents 17-6 in their last three games (3-0-0).

home.name: Carter Hart
home.news: The Golden Knights have rotated goalies in recent games, but they will turn to Hart on Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Lightning. Hart was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 28 of 30 shots (.933 SV%) in a 6-2 win over the Calgary Flames. The 28-year-old Canadian goalie has a 2.35 GAA and .911 SV% in six games (4-2-0). The Golden Knights enter Tuesday's matchup as slight -102 home underdogs against a Tampa Bay Lightning team that is 6-1-0 in their last seven games.
